title: Plans, Wishes, and Appointments
summary: Plans, wishes, appointments, devices, and everyday scheduling.
whyItMatters: Everyday planning connects intentions to concrete dates, times, contacts, and reminders. This vocabulary helps you explain what you want to do, record an appointment, and manage simple schedule changes.

mentalModel.title: Turn a wish into a calendar entry
mentalModel.content: Move from an idea to an action, then add a date, time, place, and contact person.

mentalModel.title: Separate flexible plans from fixed appointments
mentalModel.content: A plan can still change; an appointment normally has agreed details that must be confirmed or rescheduled.

mentalModel.title: Use devices as planning tools
mentalModel.content: Connect phone and calendar vocabulary to actions such as anrufen, schreiben, speichern, erinnern, and absagen.

ruleBlocks.title: Build a complete plan
ruleBlocks.content: State the activity and add when, where, and with whom: 'Ich besuche am Samstag mit Lea das Museum.'

ruleBlocks.title: Record appointment details
ruleBlocks.content: Keep the day, clock time, place, and contact together so the appointment can be confirmed or changed.

ruleBlocks.title: Connect devices to planning actions
ruleBlocks.content: Use chunks such as einen Termin speichern, eine Nachricht schreiben, jemanden anrufen, and eine Erinnerung einstellen.

ruleBlocks.title: Mark changes explicitly
ruleBlocks.content: Use verschieben, absagen, bestätigen, früher, später, and neuer Termin when a plan changes.

tables.title: Appointment Actions
rows: Ich bestätige den Termin per Nachricht.
Bitte notieren Sie die neue Uhrzeit.

patterns: einen Termin vereinbaren / bestätigen / verschieben / absagen
sentenceStructure: Use present tense with a future time expression for many plans.
Place the time early when it organizes the message: 'Am Dienstag habe ich einen Termin.'
Keep the key appointment details close together.
Use modal verbs or 'wollen' to distinguish possibility from intention.

concepts: distinguish tentative, intended, and confirmed plans

comparisons.summary: The grammar lesson supplies the forms for intentions, desired actions, and changes of state.
The communication lesson turns planning vocabulary into complete scheduling and rescheduling exchanges.

examples.de: Ich habe am Dienstag um zehn Uhr einen Termin.
examples.en: I have an appointment on Tuesday at ten.

examples.de: Mein Wunsch ist eine Reise nach Wien.
examples.en: My wish is a trip to Vienna.

examples.de: Bitte schicken Sie mir eine Nachricht mit der neuen Uhrzeit.
examples.en: Please send me a message with the new time.

examples.de: Ich speichere den Termin im Kalender und stelle eine Erinnerung ein.
examples.en: I save the appointment in the calendar and set a reminder.

examples.de: Der Termin am Freitag fällt aus; wir brauchen einen neuen Termin.
examples.en: Friday's appointment is cancelled; we need a new appointment.

commonMistakes.correct: Wir treffen uns am Dienstag um 10 Uhr im Büro.
commonMistakes.reason: A usable appointment needs concrete details.

commonMistakes.correct: der Termin = appointment or scheduled date/time

commonMistakes.wrong: Cancel without discussing what happens next.
commonMistakes.correct: State the cancellation and propose or request a new time.
commonMistakes.reason: The planning task remains incomplete without a next step.

specialCases: German often uses the present tense plus a future time expression for planned events.
'Verabredung' is often a social arrangement, while 'Termin' is common for formal or service appointments.
'Ausfallen' means an event does not take place; 'absagen' is what a person does to cancel it.
tips: Practice with a real weekly calendar.
Say every appointment as day, time, place, and purpose.
Create paired messages: original appointment and changed appointment.
